newsitem.title: JAPAN: EU's Fischler urges higher grain set-aside rate.
newsitem.headline: EU's Fischler urges higher grain set-aside rate.

text.p: European Union (EU) Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Tuesday that the EU's grain set-aside rate for 1997/98 should be raised because of higher crop output in 1996.
"It's clearly necessary to increase the set-aside rate for the next marketing year," Fischler told reporters in Makuhari, Chiba, where an international food exhibition is being held this week.
The EU's grain output was expected to have reached a record 202 million tonnes in 1996, around 27 million tonnes higher than in 1995.
The EU last summer halved the cereals set-aside rate to five percent for the 1997 harvest after public stocks fell to the lowest level for many years and prices soared.

Fischler said last week in Brussels that EU grain production was increasing at an "alarming" rate, and added a choice would have to be made between either increasing set-aside rates or removing export refunds.
But Fischler also said it was still too early to propose a set-aside rate for 1997/98.
"The decision (on the set-aside rate) is usually made in July. So before we have firm estimates of the harvest we can't fix the set-aside rate," Fischler said.
